B03_00: Coagulation is initiated when injury or inflammation exposes tissue factor, normally cryptic on fibroblasts, smooth muscle cells and pericytes, which binds factor VIIa and activates factors IX and X to generate an initial thrombin burst. Cofactors carry the signal forward while TFPI, antithrombin and protein S on heparan sulfate proteoglycans restrain it. Ectopic tissue factor drives thrombosis and DIC, and FVIII or FIX deficiency causes haemophilia.
B03_01: Platelet degranulation releases granule cargo at vessel injury to amplify platelet recruitment, support coagulation and initiate repair; defects cause gray platelet and storage pool disease. Alpha granules supply von Willebrand factor, fibrinogen, factor V, serpins and growth factors such as PDGF, TGF-beta and VEGF, while P-selectin and CD63 appear on the surface. Fusion depends on SNARE and regulatory proteins, coupled to integrin activation.
B03_02: Rising cytosolic calcium converts agonist binding into responses in non-excitable cells, driving platelet shape change, secretion, integrin activation and aggregation. IP3 opens ER channels to release stores; STIM1 senses depletion and gates ORAI1/ORAI2 for store-operated entry, while P2X and TRPC channels admit calcium directly. STIM1 or ORAI1 loss causes immunodeficiency and impaired platelet activation, while excessive entry favours thrombosis.
B03_03: After a calcium transient, cells clear cytosolic calcium using SERCA pumps to refill stores, plasma membrane calcium ATPases, and high-capacity sodium/calcium exchangers dominant in cardiac myocytes. Calmodulin stimulates the membrane pumps for feedback control, and sorcin modulates handling in excitable cells. Restoring resting calcium sets muscle relaxation, resets neurons and secretory cells and prevents overload-induced death; failure contributes to heart failure, arrhythmia and hereditary deafness.
B03_04: GRB2 and SOS1 couple integrin adhesion complexes to Ras, converting matrix attachment into MAP kinase proliferative and survival signals. In activated platelets, fibrinogen, fibronectin and von Willebrand factor engage talin-bound ITGA2B/ITGB3, activated upstream via RAP1 and APBB1IP. Clustering activates FAK and SRC, which recruit GRB2-SOS; without this link, cells remain attached but lack ERK output needed for anchorage-dependent growth, migration and aggregation.
B03_05: Thrombin cleaves proteinase-activated receptors, unmasking a tethered ligand that irreversibly activates them, turning a clotting signal into cellular responses. In platelets this drives shape change, secretion, integrin activation and aggregation, central to haemostasis and arterial thrombosis, and it also acts on endothelium, smooth muscle and inflammatory cells. Gq and G12/13 coupling activates PLC beta, calcium, PKC and Rho, while beta-arrestins terminate signalling; PAR1 dominates, with PAR4.
B03_06: Endothelial prostacyclin acting on the Gs-coupled receptor PTGIR keeps platelets quiescent and vessels relaxed, the main brake on spontaneous thrombosis. Via GNAS and beta-gamma subunits, it activates adenylate cyclase, raising cAMP and PKA activity to block the calcium rise needed for platelet activation, and relaxes smooth muscle. It opposes thromboxane A2, and loss of prostacyclin tone contributes to pulmonary arterial hypertension and thrombotic risk.
B03_07: In the contact system, surface-autoactivated factor XII activates factor XI, and kallikrein from kininogen-bound prekallikrein can activate factor IX, amplifying fibrin formation and linking coagulation to kinin inflammation. It is dispensable for haemostasis yet drives pathological thrombosis, making it an attractive antithrombotic target, while C1 inhibitor deficiency raises risk. Assembly occurs on platelet GPIb-IX-V, and factor XI deficiency, unlike factor XII deficiency, causes bleeding.
B03_08: Thromboxane A2, a platelet eicosanoid, drives aggregation and vasoconstriction through the TP receptor, contributing to thrombosis, hypertension and bronchoconstriction, and blocking its production or receptor is standard cardiovascular prophylaxis. TP has two splice variants differing in their tails. Gq coupling activates phospholipase C and calcium for shape change and granule release, while G13 activates Rho and Rac for cytoskeletal remodelling.
B03_09: At normal plasma levels, LDL lowers platelet activation thresholds, enhancing aggregation to thrombin, collagen or ADP and linking dyslipidaemia to atherosclerotic thrombosis. ApoB binds ApoER2 (LRP8), recruiting Fgr and activating p38 MAP kinase, which phosphorylates cytosolic phospholipase A2 to release arachidonate for thromboxane. LDL also triggers PECAM-1 signalling, recruiting SHP-1, SHP-2 and PP2A to dephosphorylate p38 and end priming.
B03_10: The endothelial receptor tyrosine kinase Tie2 (TEK) signals vessels to remain quiescent, connected and alive. Angiopoietin-1 and -4 activate it, while angiopoietin-2 competes, priming sprouting or regression, balancing vascular stability, permeability and angiogenesis in development, wound healing and tumours. Phosphorylated Tie2 recruits SHC1, GRB2-SOS1 and PTPN11 for MAP kinase signalling and PI3K for AKT survival; mutations cause venous malformations.
B03_11: The platelet GPIb-IX-V complex (GP1BA, GP1BB, GP9, GP5) binds von Willebrand factor on exposed subendothelial collagen under high arterial shear, tethering platelets for adhesion and activation. Its loss causes Bernard-Soulier syndrome with giant platelets and bleeding, while engagement at ruptured plaques drives heart attack and stroke. Its tail signals via filamin A, Src, PI3K and 14-3-3, and it presents thrombin to PARs.
B03_12: Platelet granule release requires freeing syntaxin-4 from Munc18-3 (STXBP3), which holds it closed and unable to form SNARE complexes. Conventional PKC isoforms activated by thrombin, collagen and other agonists phosphorylate the pair, letting syntaxin-4 assemble with SNAP and VAMP partners to drive dense and alpha granule exocytosis, amplifying aggregation. Similar control governs insulin and immune granule release, and defective secretion causes bleeding.
B03_13: Basigin (CD147) is an immunoglobulin-superfamily glycoprotein acting as an adhesion receptor and chaperone for transporters, setting surface levels of lactate-exporting monocarboxylate transporters. Engagement on fibroblasts induces metalloproteinases and VEGF, supporting tumour invasion and metastasis. Partners include 4F2hc with amino acid exchangers, Na+/K+-ATPase beta, caveolin-1, beta1 integrins, cyclophilin A, L1CAM, MAG and basigin itself, linking adhesion, metabolism, migration and development.
B03_14: Collagen binding by platelet GPVI triggers shape change, secretion and aggregation, initiating haemostasis and driving arterial thrombosis. GPVI pairs with FcR gamma, whose ITAM is phosphorylated by Fyn and Lyn to recruit Syk and assemble a LAT-SLP-76 signalosome, leading through PI3K and PLC-gamma2 to calcium and PKC, and through VAV to Rac, RhoA and CDC42. CLEC-2 shares this machinery; GPVI blockade is an antithrombotic strategy.
B03_15: This branch converts integrin-matrix adhesion into MAP kinase growth and motility signals. Platelet alphaIIb-beta3 clustering on fibrinogen, fibronectin or von Willebrand factor, stabilised by talin, Rap1 and RIAM, assembles a FAK-Src complex that phosphorylates p130Cas to recruit Crk, coupling adhesion to Ras-ERK and Rac. Outputs include spreading, migration, aggregation and clot retraction; defects cause bleeding, and tumour cells exploit the axis.
B03_16: In amplification and propagation, initial thrombin activates factors XI, VIII and V on platelets, where tenase (FIXa-FVIIIa) produces FXa and prothrombinase (FXa-FVa) cleaves prothrombin, generating cross-linked fibrin that stabilises the plug. ANO6-dependent phosphatidylserine exposure and von Willebrand factor binding via GPIb-IX-V support this. Antithrombin, heparin cofactor II and protein C/S restrain it; FVIII or FIX loss causes haemophilia, defective inhibition thrombosis.
B03_17: ADP released from platelet dense granules acts on the P2Y12 receptor to convert reversible clumps into stable thrombi, required for aggregation by all agonists and targeted by thienopyridine drugs after stenting; loss-of-function variants cause bleeding. P2RY12 couples to Gi, lowering adenylate cyclase output and cAMP to relieve PKA restraint on calcium, while beta-gamma acts separately. Effects include secretion, thromboxane generation and integrin activation.
B03_18: cGMP produced in response to nitric oxide or natriuretic peptides relaxes smooth muscle, restrains platelets and tunes neuronal excitability. cGMP-dependent kinases PRKG1 and PRKG2 lower cytosolic calcium by phosphorylating IRAG1 with the IP3 receptor and activating BK potassium channels. Phosphodiesterases such as PDE5A terminate signalling, and PDE5 inhibitors treat erectile dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension; loss favours vasoconstriction and platelet aggregation.
B03_19: Diacylglycerol lipases alpha and beta hydrolyse arachidonate-rich DAG to produce 2-arachidonoylglycerol, the main brain endocannabinoid, which acts on CB1 to suppress synaptic neurotransmitter release. Monoacylglycerol lipase, ABHD6 and ABHD12 degrade 2-AG to glycerol and arachidonate, ending signalling and supplying eicosanoid precursors. This balance links lipid signalling to inflammation, pain and neuroprotection; ABHD12 loss causes neurodegeneration with ataxia and retinitis pigmentosa.
B03_20: Platelet-released ADP acts on the P2Y1 receptor to initiate shape change and reversible aggregation, working with P2Y12, the clopidogrel target; both are needed for irreversible aggregation, so loss causes bleeding and excess favours arterial thrombosis. P2Y1 couples to Gq-family subunits to mobilise stored calcium, and p38 and Src signalling activate cytosolic phospholipase A2 for thromboxane synthesis, linking nucleotide sensing to integrin activation and clotting.
B03_21: PECAM-1 (CD31), an immunoglobulin-superfamily receptor at endothelial junctions and on platelets and leukocytes, governs transendothelial migration, T cell activation, platelet responses and angiogenesis through homophilic and integrin binding. Src-family kinases phosphorylate its ITIMs, recruiting SHP-1, SHP-2 and SHIP1 to dampen immunoreceptor and integrin signalling. This sets activation thresholds, while junctional PECAM-1 maintains the barrier and senses shear, linking it to inflammation and thrombosis.
B03_22: Adrenaline acting on three alpha-2 adrenergic receptor subtypes couples to Gi/Go to inhibit adenylate cyclase and lower cAMP, while released subunits regulate potassium and calcium channels. Effects include suppressed insulin and increased glucagon secretion, gastrointestinal sphincter contraction, platelet aggregation and presynaptic autoinhibition of noradrenaline release. This feedback explains how clonidine and dexmedetomidine reduce sympathetic outflow, blood pressure and produce sedation.
B03_23: Fibrin formation converts soluble fibrinogen into an insoluble meshwork that seals wounds and strengthens clots. Thrombin removes fibrinopeptides so monomers assemble into fibers, which calcium-dependent factor XIIIa cross-links against breakdown, and platelet alphaIIb-beta3 binds the network for retraction. Antithrombin, heparin cofactor II and protein C keep deposition local; fibrinogen or factor XIII deficiency causes bleeding, while losing inhibition predisposes to thrombosis.
